\section[\texorpdfstring{\ja{どうして} (doushite)}{どうして (doushite)}]{\ja{どうして} (doushite) — why}

\label{lesson:JA-C98-doushite}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Japanese for a method, then the Japanese for a way of doing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ja{どうして}}
\textbf{\ja{どうして}} — \emph{doushite} — \textquotedblleft{}why\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ja{どうして}} (\emph{dōshite}) is native: \emph{dō}, \textquotedblleft{}how\textquotedblright{}, built on the \emph{do-} of \textquotedblleft{}which\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{shite}, the linking form of \emph{suru}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}: \textquotedblleft{}having done how\textquotedblright{} (JMdict). It is inherited rather than borrowed.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Japanese for a method, then the Japanese for a way of doing, then say \emph{doushite} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ja{りゆう} (riyuu)}{りゆう (riyuu)}]{\ja{りゆう} (riyuu) — a reason}

\label{lesson:JA-C98-riyuu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Japanese for a way of doing, then the Japanese for why.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ja{りゆう}}
\textbf{\ja{りゆう}} — \emph{riyuu} — \textquotedblleft{}a reason\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ja{りゆう}} (\emph{riyuu}) is Sino-Japanese (kango): two Chinese characters read with their on'yomi, readings borrowed from Chinese. They are \emph{ri}, \textquotedblleft{}reason\textquotedblright{} (Middle Chinese \emph{liX}) and \emph{yū}, \textquotedblleft{}cause\textquotedblright{} (\emph{yuw}) (Unihan, KANJIDIC2; Middle Chinese after Baxter–Sagart).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ja{ため} (tame)}{ため (tame)}]{\ja{ため} (tame) — for the sake of; because of}

\label{lesson:JA-C98-tame}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Japanese for why, then the Japanese for a reason.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ja{ため}}
\textbf{\ja{ため}} — \emph{tame} — \textquotedblleft{}for the sake of; because of\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ja{ため}} (\emph{tame}) is a native Japanese word, inherited rather than borrowed from Chinese, and its older origin is not settled. It is usually written in kana; its kanji, when used, is a kun'yomi attached later (JMdict, KANJIDIC2).
\end{cousinweb}
